## Review

**7 out of 10, Effective.** Presentation quality, judged with the SlideDeck Co review heuristic (https://slidedeck.co/review-methodology/). The ask, the evidence and the merit of the idea are not rated.

Each content slide has a headline in the blue band that states the takeaway with a directional word (slide 8, 'Solid But Slowing +6% vs. +7% Y/Y'), followed by one large chart in a consistent template. Sections are signposted by divider slides (7, 18, 22, 37, 41), so the route through the 72 pages I saw is easy to follow, and the later paired image and chart slides (58 to 71) use an effective repeated pattern. Weaknesses are consequential: axis labels, tick values and footnotes are pale grey and tiny (slide 8), several slides are dense or small (the tables on 14 and 15, the 6-paragraph text on 5 and 6), and about a dozen section dividers and empty blue-band slides add low-content pages. The deck reads well as a report but is hard to present on a screen, which holds it at competent.

**Worth keeping:** Keep the takeaway headline in the blue band over a single large chart, the consistent colour coding and the repeating image plus chart plus quote layout on slides 58 to 71.

**Most useful repair:** Raise the contrast and size of axis labels and tick values (slide 8), and break the text-only context slides 5 and 6 into short statements.

**What would change the score:** Cut or merge the stand-alone divider slides (18, 22, 37, 41, 43, 44, 46) and replace the dense market-cap tables on 14 and 15 with a simpler ranked chart.

_Confidence medium. 72 of 334 pages inspected on contact sheets, 4 at readable size. Reviewed Reviewed 2026-11-08. Model-assisted review (claude-sonnet-5-5)._

## Summary

Internet Trends 2019 is a data-heavy talk by Mary Meeker of Bond, presented at Code 2019 on June 11. It opens with a title slide, a Bond branded cover, an agenda listing eleven sections, and a thanks slide crediting contributors, including Hillhouse Capital for the China section. A context section then frames the report around data, consumer and regulator concerns, and the roles of commerce, advertising and usage. The main body moves through users and smartphone shipments, then e-commerce and online advertising, followed by usage topics such as gaming, video, voice, images and on-demand services. Later sections cover non-US internet businesses, data-driven fulfillment and financial services. The deck relies on large single-metric charts with headline-style titles, each stating the takeaway with a directional word such as solid, slowing or accelerating. Slides with bar and line combinations and short quoted executive comments give the sections their rhythm. It closes with the China section and the remaining sections, and the final slides point to specific companies as examples.

## Questions about this deck

**What does the Bond Internet Trends 2019 deck say about the structure of the deck and its agenda?**

Slide 3 is the agenda, listing eleven sections from 1) Users through 11) China (Provided by Hillhouse Capital). The deck opens with a title slide on Slide 1 and closes with the China section and the remaining sections, according to its summary.

**What does Mary Meeker's Bond Internet Trends 2019 deck say about e-commerce growth?**

Slide 19, titled E-Commerce Growth, reads Solid +12.4% vs. +12.1% (Y/Y, Q1 vs. Q4). The chart on that slide shows E-Commerce Sales vs. Y/Y Growth, USA.

**What does the Bond Internet Trends 2019 deck say about internet advertising spending?**

Slide 24, titled Internet Ad Spending (Annual), is headlined Accelerated +22% vs. +21% Y/Y. The chart on that slide shows Internet Advertising Spend, USA, with a Y/Y Growth line, and cites IAB / PwC data.

**What does the Bond Internet Trends 2019 deck say about market capitalization leaders?**

Slide 13, titled Global Internet Market Capitalization Leaders, is headlined USA Stable @ 18 of 30 and China Stable @ 7 of 30. The slide's table ranks companies by market cap value on 6/7/19 and 6/7/16 with a % Change column.

### Slide 5

**Review notes**

- Suggested repair: Raise the contrast and size of axis labels and tick values (slide 8), and break the text-only context slides 5 and 6 into short statements.

**Text**

Context…
We use data to tell stories of business-related trends we focus on. We hope others take the ideas, build
on them & make them better.
At 3.8B, the number of Internet users comprises more than half the world’s population. When markets
reach mainstream, new growth is harder to find as evinced by declining new smartphone shipments in
2018. While E-Commerce continues to gain share vs. physical retail, growth rates are slowing. While
Internet advertising growth is solid & innovation is healthy, there are areas where customer acquisition
costs may be rising to unsustainable levels.
While Internet user growth is slowing, global innovation & competition continue to drive product
improvements, new types of usage & monetization – especially in areas of digital video, voice,
wearables, on-demand + local services & traditionally underserved markets. Outside of USA, we focus
on especially high growth & innovation in data-driven / direct fulfillment & financial services. We highlight
massive global usage changes related to the evolution of images & interactive gaming as
communications tools & the broad emergence of freemium businesses at scale.
The rapid rise of gathered / analyzed digital data is often core to the holistic success of the fastest
growing & most successful companies of our time around the world. Context-rich data can help
businesses provide consumers with increasingly personalized products & services that can often be
obtained at lower prices & delivered more efficiently. This, in turn, can drive higher customer satisfaction.
Better data-driven tools can improve the ability for consumers to communicate directly & indirectly with
businesses & regulators.
Core constituents (consumers / businesses / regulators) are increasingly drinking from a data firehose &
management challenges continue to rise for all parties. Broad awareness of challenges (& related
vigorous / heated debates) can be the first step in driving change.
BOND
Internet Trends
2019
4

### Slide 6

**Review notes**

- Suggested repair: Raise the contrast and size of axis labels and tick values (slide 8), and break the text-only context slides 5 and 6 into short statements.

**Text**

...Context
Consumers are aware of concerns about Internet usage overload & are taking steps to reduce usage –
leading USA-based Internet platforms have rolled out tools to help monitor usage & social media usage
growth appears to be decelerating following a period of strong growth. Privacy & problematic content
concerns are also top-of-mind & are following similar patterns.
Owing to social media amplification, reveals / actions / reactions about events can occur quickly –
resulting in both good & bad outcomes. In markets where online real-time rating systems exist,
accountability can be improved vs. offline options as consumers & businesses interact directly while
regulators can also benefit.
Rapidly expanding connectivity has helped amplify voices of good & bad actors. This has brought new
focus to an age-old challenge for regulators around the world – finding the most effective ways to amplify
good & minimize bad, often resulting in different regional interpretations & strategies.
As Internet systems become increasingly sophisticated, data-rich & mission critical, so has the opportunity
for cyber attacks. We are in a new era of cyber security where technology issues are increasingly
intermixed with international diplomacy & defense.
We focus on the impact of the Internet on work (via on-demand services & remote options), education &
healthcare – the materiality of current trends imply inflections are occurring. We update USA trending
around government finances & the importance of immigration to the technology sector.
The Hillhouse Capital team provides insights into China – the largest market of Internet users & a leader
in innovation / scale.
5
Internet Trends
2019
BOND

### Slide 8

**Review notes**

- Worth studying: A combined bar and line chart with a clear headline stating the takeaway (solid but slowing growth) and a single visual focus.
- Review: Each content slide has a headline in the blue band that states the takeaway with a directional word (slide 8, 'Solid But Slowing +6% vs.
- Review: Weaknesses are consequential: axis labels, tick values and footnotes are pale grey and tiny (slide 8), several slides are dense or small (the tables on 14 and 15, the 6-paragraph text on 5 and 6), and about a dozen section dividers and empty blue-band slides add low-content pages.
- Suggested repair: Raise the contrast and size of axis labels and tick values (slide 8), and break the text-only context slides 5 and 6 into short statements.

**Layout**

Full-width slide with a solid dark-blue title band across the top (0 to 12.5% of height) carrying a left-aligned two-line white title, with a single centred chart title below it. The horizontal bar chart fills the centre column, category labels right-aligned against the zero axis, bars growing rightwards, with the legend centred below the axis label. A thin light-grey rule runs across the footer; the BOND wordmark and 'Internet Trends 2019' sit bottom-left, the centred three-line source note bottom-centre and the page number '10' bottom-right, with margins of about 2 to 4% of the width.

**Visuals**

Chart: horizontal stacked bar chart, title 'Internet Users by Region, 2018'. Value axis labelled 'Population' runs from 0 to 6B with tick labels 0, 3B and 6B (light grey, #BFBFBF), vertical light-grey gridlines (#D9D9D9) at 0, 3B and 6B. Category axis lists five regions top to bottom: Asia Pacific, Europe, Africa & Middle East, Latin America & Caribbean, North America. Two stacked series: Internet Users (dark blue #00517A, first segment) and Non-Internet Users (light grey #D9D9D9, second segment). Estimated values, read against the axis (no numeric bar values printed, so about): Asia Pacific Internet Users about 2.0B, Non-Internet Users about 2.2B, total about 4.2B; Europe about 0.6B and about 0.15B; Africa & Middle East about 0.5B and about 1.1B; Latin America & Caribbean about 0.4B and about 0.2B; North America about 0.3B and about 0.03B. Printed labels beside each bar, two lines each: Asia Pacific '53% of Global Internet Users' and '48% Internet User Penetration in Region'; Europe '15%' and '78%'; Africa & Middle East '13%' and '32%'; Latin America & Caribbean '10%' and '62%'; North America '9%' and '89%'. No bars are highlighted. Legend below the axis: dark blue square then 'Internet Users', light grey square then 'Non-Internet Users'. Logo: small grey BOND wordmark (serif, bottom-left), image about 60 by 15 pixels.

**Design**

Background white #FFFFFF. Title band solid #00517A with white #FFFFFF title text in Arial regular, about 4.4% of slide height per line, sentence case, left aligned. Chart title in Arial bold, about 3.7% of height, dark slate #3E464E for 'Internet Users by Region,' and near-black #2A3137 for '2018'. Category labels and data labels in Arial bold #2A3137 at about 2.6% (category) and Arial regular #2A3137 about 2.2% for the chart end labels and 1.3% for the stacked value labels. Axis tick and axis title text Arial regular #BFBFBF at about 1.8%. Legend text Arial regular #2A3137 at about 2.2%. Footer text Arial regular #BFBFBF at about 1.3%, page number Arial regular #A6A6A6 about 1.5%, BOND wordmark in grey serif, 'Internet Trends' in Georgia #C8C8C8 at about 1.5%, '2019' Georgia #C8C8C8. Shapes are flat with no shadows, no gradients, square corners; bars have thin white separators between the two segments; footer divider is a hairline light grey.

**Text**

Global Internet Users = / China @ 21% of Total...India @ 12%...USA @ 8% / Internet Users – Top Countries, 2018 / China / India / United States / Indonesia / Brazil / Japan / Russia / Mexico / Germany / The Philippines / United Kingdom / Iran (I.R.) / Nigeria / France / Turkey / 0 / 0.8B / 1.6B / Internet Users / Non-Internet Users / BOND / Internet Trends / 2019 / Internet user data is as of mid-year. Pew Research (USA), China Internet Network Information Center (China), Islamic Republic News Agency / / InternetWorldStats / Bond estimates (Iran), Bond estimates based on IAMAI data (India), & APJII (Indonesia). / 11

**Layout**

Full-width navy title band across the top about 12.5% of the slide height, with a two-line left-aligned white title inside it starting at about 1.9% from the left edge. A single chart occupies the middle: centred bold chart title, then horizontal bars with category labels right-aligned in a column left of the axis, vertical gridlines, an x-axis label row, and a centred legend below. A thin light grey rule runs across the slide at about 93% height above a three-part footer: BOND wordmark and 'Internet Trends 2019' at the left margin, a centred grey source block, and the page number at the right margin.

**Visuals**

Horizontal stacked bar chart titled 'Internet Users – Top Countries, 2018'. X-axis: units are billions of people (labels 0, 0.8B, 1.6B), with vertical light grey gridlines at 0, 0.8B and 1.6B; the axis runs from 0 to about 1.6B and the plot extends slightly past 1.6B. Y-axis: 15 countries listed top to bottom in this order: China, India, United States, Indonesia, Brazil, Japan, Russia, Mexico, Germany, The Philippines, United Kingdom, Iran (I.R.), Nigeria, France, Turkey. Two stacked series per bar: Internet Users (navy #00517A, left segment) and Non-Internet Users (light grey #D9D9D9, right segment). No values are printed on the bars; estimates follow, marked about. China: Internet Users about 0.80B, Non-Internet about 0.58B, total about 1.38B. India: Internet Users about 0.45B, Non-Internet about 0.84B, total about 1.29B. United States: about 0.29B and about 0.04B, total about 0.33B. Indonesia: about 0.17B and about 0.09B, total about 0.26B. Brazil: about 0.14B and about 0.07B, total about 0.21B. Japan: about 0.11B and about 0.01B, total about 0.12B. Russia: about 0.11B and about 0.03B, total about 0.14B. Mexico: about 0.08B and about 0.05B, total about 0.13B. Germany: about 0.07B and about 0.01B, total about 0.08B. The Philippines: about 0.06B and about 0.04B, total about 0.10B. United Kingdom: about 0.06B, no visible grey segment. Iran (I.R.): about 0.05B and about 0.03B, total about 0.08B. Nigeria: about 0.06B and about 0.14B, total about 0.20B. France: about 0.05B and about 0.02B, total about 0.07B. Turkey: about 0.05B and about 0.03B, total about 0.08B. Legend: navy square labelled Internet Users, light grey square labelled Non-Internet Users, in a horizontal row below the axis. No highlighted points. Sorted in descending order of total users. Also a BOND wordmark logo bottom left, a small grey rule across the footer, and no photographs or icons.

**Design**

Background white #FFFFFF. Title band solid navy #00517A spanning full width, with title text in white #FFFFFF in regular Arial/Helvetica-style sans-serif, about 4.4% of slide height per line, left aligned, two lines. Chart title in bold Arial/Helvetica sans-serif, dark slate #3E464E, about 3.7% of slide height, centred. Category labels in regular Arial, dark charcoal #2A3137, about 2.2% of slide height, right aligned. Axis tick labels in regular Arial, light grey #BFBFBF, about 1.8% of slide height. Legend text regular Arial #2A3137 about 2.2%. Bars are flat with no outline, no shadows, no gradients; navy #00517A and light grey #D9D9D9; thin white separator between navy and grey segments. Gridlines thin light grey #D9D9D9 vertical lines. Footer text regular Arial #BFBFBF about 1.3% of slide height, centred source block. BOND logo in grey serif #A6A6A6-toned lettering; 'Internet Trends' and '2019' in Georgia serif, light grey #C8C8C8, about 1.5% of slide height. Page number in Arial #A6A6A6 about 1.5%. Thin footer rule light grey #E5E5E5.

Combined bar and line chart. Title: 'E-Commerce Sales vs. Y/Y Growth, USA' (bold). Left axis titled 'E-Commerce Sales (Blue Bar)' in $ billions, range $0 to $140B with gridlines at $0, $70B and $140B. Right axis titled 'Y/Y Growth (Red Line)' in percent, range 0% to 20% with labels at 0%, 10% and 20%. Series 1, bars: 37 quarterly bars from Q1 2010 to Q1 2019, dark blue, rising steadily; no values printed, so estimates: Q1 2010 about $39B, Q1 2019 about $138B (the tallest bar). Series 2, red line (Y/Y growth): starts around Q2 2010 at about 17%, peaks near Q1 2011 at about 19.5%, falls to about 10% around Q1 2013 and about 11% in 2014, rises to about 14% by Q4 2017 and drops to about 12% by Q4 2018, ending at about 12.4% at Q1 2019. Quarter labels Q1 to Q4 sit under each bar, grouped under year labels 2010 to 2019 with short light grey underline brackets. Legend: none; series are identified by axis titles. **Layout**

Full-slide white canvas with a full-width dark teal title band across the top (about 12.5% of slide height) carrying a two-line left-aligned white title starting at about 1.7% from the left edge. Below the band, a centred bold chart subtitle sits above two side-by-side grouped bar charts (2010 left, 2018 right) separated by a thin vertical grey divider at about x 50%; each chart has its year heading centred above it, a y-axis at left with a 0% to 50% scale and category labels beneath. **Visuals**

Grouped vertical bar chart pair. Chart 1 title 2010 and chart 2 title 2018, both bold. Y axis labelled % of Time Spent in Media / Advertising Spending, 2010, USA (left chart) and % of Time Spent in Media / Advertising Spending, 2018, USA (right chart); scale 0% to 50% with gridlines at 0%, 25% and 50%; light grey gridlines. X categories: Print, Radio, TV, Desktop, Mobile. Each category has two bars: Time Spent (deep maroon #640F2A, or light pink #E03169 at 25% opacity for Print, Radio and TV) and Ad Spend (dark teal #00517A, or pale blue-grey #00517A at 25% opacity for Print, Radio and TV). 2010 values: Time Spent Print 8%, Radio 16%, TV 43%, Desktop 25%, Mobile 8%; Ad Spend Print 27%, Radio 11%, TV 43%, Desktop 19%, Mobile 0.5%. 2018 values: Time Spent Print 3%, Radio 12%, TV 34%, Desktop 18%, Mobile 33%; Ad Spend Print 7%, Radio 8%, TV 34%, Desktop 18%, Mobile 33%. Data labels sit above the bars for Desktop and Mobile in dark text and inside the top of the lighter bars in small grey-green text for other categories. Desktop and Mobile categories are bold. Legend: maroon square with Time Spent and teal square with Ad Spend, both small squares. A logo image (BOND) sits bottom left, approximately 60 by 15 pixels.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background. Title band dark teal #00517A with white ArialMT regular title text, about 4.4% of slide height per line. **Text**

A hairline rule runs across the slide above a footer: BOND logo and 'Internet Trends 2019' text at bottom left, a centred two-line source note, and the page number 38 at bottom right, all with margins of about 2 to 4%.

**Visuals**

One chart and one photograph. Chart: combination column and line chart titled 'Xandr Revenue vs. Growth Y/Y' (grey #BFBFBF, centred above plot). Primary left axis labelled 'Xandr Revenue (Blue Bars)' in $MM, range $0 to $600MM with a gridline at $300MM. Secondary right axis labelled 'Y/Y Growth (Red Line)' in %, range 0% to 60% with the 30% level aligned to the $300MM gridline. Category axis: quarters Q1 to Q4 for 2017, Q1 to Q4 for 2018, and Q1 for 2019, with year labels 2017, 2018 and 2019 under grouped brackets. Blue series (#00517A) values, all about (no values printed): Q1 2017 about $320MM; Q2 2017 about $340MM; Q3 2017 about $335MM; Q4 2017 about $380MM; Q1 2018 about $335MM; Q2 2018 about $390MM; Q3 2018 about $445MM; Q4 2018 about $565MM (highest bar); Q1 2019 about $425MM. Red series (#C00000) growth, all about: Q1 2018 about 5%; Q2 2018 about 16%; Q3 2018 about 31%; Q4 2018 about 49% (peak, highlighted by the peak point); Q1 2019 about 27%. The red line has no marker points and is not drawn before Q1 2018. No legend; series identified by axis titles. Photograph (boxed, not cropped, not full-bleed): a man in a dark jacket and dark jeans with brown leather shoes reclines on a wooden floor against a dark cabinet, looking down at a lit smartphone held in his right hand. Mounted on the white wall at upper left is a flat-screen TV showing a green baseball-style field with players and a scrolling caption band. Foreground has a white tissue box and grey round low tables or stools. Framing is a wide interior shot with the man at lower right and the TV at upper left. Lighting is ambient indoor light with a bright blue glow from the phone screen. Dominant colours: white walls, dark grey and black, green field, navy denim, warm brown floor. The photo sits inside a thin dark charcoal frame border.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate report style. Background is plain white. Header band fill #00517A (dark teal blue) with white title text. Typefaces: Arial (sans-serif) regular for titles, body and chart labels; Arial Bold for subheadings, percentage figures, quarter and year labels and the Nielsen heading. Title text about 4.4% of slide height; body and stat lines about 2.6%; subheadings about 2.4%; chart labels about 1.8%; footer about 1.3% to 1.5%. **Layout**

A full-width dark blue title band fills the top 12.5% of the slide, with a two-line left-aligned title inside it starting at about 1.9% from the left. Below it a centred bold chart title sits above a single stacked column chart that spans about 20% to 80% of the width, with the y-axis label at the left and the legend centred beneath the x-axis. A thin footer rule runs across the slide near 93% of its height; the BOND Internet Trends logo block sits bottom-left, a centred three-line source and note block sits bottom-centre, and the page number 41 sits bottom-right at about 96.5% from the left.

**Visuals**

Stacked column chart, titled Daily Hours Spent with Digital Media per Adult User, USA. Y-axis: labelled Hours Spent per Day, USA, range 0 to 8 with labelled gridlines at 0, 4 and 8 (light grey horizontal lines). X-axis: years 2008 to 2018, one column per year. Three stacked series from bottom to top: Other Connected Devices (dark blue #00517A) with values 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.4, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7 for 2008 to 2018; Desktop / Laptop (light grey #BFBFBF) with values 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6, 2.5, 2.3, 2.2, 2.2, 2.2, 2.1, 2.0; Mobile (green #258B74) with values 0.3, 0.3, 0.4, 0.8, 1.6, 2.3, 2.6, 2.8, 3.1, 3.3, 3.6. Column total labels above each column, in dark grey: 2.7, 3.0, 3.2, 3.7, 4.3, 4.9, 5.1, 5.4, 5.6, 5.9, 6.3. Segment values are printed inside each segment, white on dark blue and green, dark grey on light grey. Legend centred below the axis: dark blue square Other Connected Devices, grey square Desktop / Laptop, green square Mobile. No highlighted points.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF covering the whole slide. White slide background. Title text is white on a #00517A dark blue band, in a regular sans-serif (Arial-like) at about 4.4% of slide height. Chart title is bold Arial-like sans-serif #3C444C at about 3.7% of slide height. Axis tick and year labels are light grey #BFBFBF at about 1.8%. Data labels are about 1.8% of slide height in Arial-like regular type, coloured #353B37 on grey and #FFFFFF on blue and green. Accent colours are #00517A (blue), #BFBFBF (grey) and #258B74 (green). Columns are flat with no shadows, gradients or rounded corners; thin white separators divide the stacked segments. Footer text is light grey #BFBFBF at about 1.3%; the BOND logo is grey serif and the Internet Trends and 2019 lines are light grey #C8C8C8 Georgia-like serif.

Full-width dark-blue title band across the top 12.5 percent of the slide, with the two-line white title left-aligned at a 1.9 percent left margin. Below the band the slide is split into two columns by a faint vertical divider near 50 percent: the left column has a centered bold heading and two phone images side by side in the middle, the right column has a centered bold heading over a stacked area chart with its legend beneath. A thin grey rule sits near 93 percent above the footer, which holds the BOND Internet Trends 2019 logo block at bottom left, a centered two-line source note, and the page number 49 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Two photographs and one chart. (1) Left photo, a Facebook Android app screenshot: status bar at top right reads 2:04 with wifi and battery icons on a blue header; blue search bar with magnifier and the word Search and a Messenger icon; navigation row of video, marketplace, notifications bell and menu icons; a Play All link; a horizontal row of story tiles showing Connor Hayes, Kai Ding (with small New Avatar Effect label) and John McLord, plus a partly cut-off tile at left; a rounded white composer field reading What's on your mind? with a Photo icon; a post by Guillermo Moreno with Josephine Williams and 2 others, timestamp Yesterday at 10:14 PM, text ending friends, good food and a lot of laughs.; a cropped photo at bottom of a group of five people seated outdoors among green shrubs with a bouquet of flowers in the centre. The screenshot is boxed inside a thin near-black rounded frame, full colour, daylight tones with blue and white UI. (2) Right photo, a selfie in an AR camera view: a woman with dark hair wearing a silver astronaut helmet with a dark visor and black chin collar, pulling a wide-eyed grimace with pursed lips; she wears a bright royal-blue top; background is a dark wall with pinned papers and a red wire at top; camera UI shows a circular arrow at top right, and at the bottom a star effect icon, flip-camera icon, large white shutter circle, flash-off icon and a gallery thumbnail; the image is cropped to a tall portrait box with a dark charcoal border, dominant colours blue, charcoal and silver. (3) Chart: stacked area chart titled Daily Active Users, Global*. Y axis titled Daily Active Users, Global, range 0 to 1.6B, labelled 0, 0.8B and 1.6B, light grey gridlines at 0.8B and 1.6B. ### Slide 58

**Review notes**

- Worth keeping: Keep the takeaway headline in the blue band over a single large chart, the consistent colour coding and the repeating image plus chart plus quote layout on slides 58 to 71.

**Text**

China (Pinduoduo) = Connecting Consumer Preferences & Manufacturers… / 443MM Buyers + ~2x in Five Quarters / Pinduoduo / Group Discovery / Buying / Active Buyers, China / 500MM / 250MM / Pinduoduo Active Buyers, China / 0 / Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 / 2017 / 2018 / 2019 / Main page – browsing and exploration / Product introduction / Product categories / Campaigns / Sales promotion / Product recommendation / Buyer A / Buyer B / Join an existing team initiated by another buyer / Initiate a team purchase / Individual purchase / We call it consumer-to-manufacturer, where we / understand the users' needs first & enable upstream / providers, be it farmers, manufacturers, etc. to / produce appropriate products for our users. / This is different from how the current system works, / where upstream producers design, manufacture & / sell without necessarily being in tune with the / changing needs of their targeted users. / As we add more users to the network & also gain more data / points through their increasing interaction with our platform, / we can further refine our engine to deliver an even better user / experience that keeps up with our users' evolving preferences. / Pinduoduo – Q4:18 Earnings Call, 3/19 / BOND / Internet Trends / 2019 / Source: Pinduoduo SEC filings (2018), Q4:18 Earnings Call (3/19) & Morgan Stanley. / Note: An active buyer is a buyer who has completed at least one transaction in the past 12 months. / 57

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top 12.5% of the slide with a two-line left-aligned white title, followed by a centred bold heading 'Pinduoduo' and two column headings: a left column (screenshot image above a centred italic quote block) and a right column (line chart) separated by a thin vertical divider at about x 50%. A thin horizontal rule sits above the footer; the footer has the BOND logo and 'Internet Trends 2019' at bottom left, centred source and note lines, and the page number 57 at bottom right with a left margin of about 4% and right margin of about 3.5%.

**Visuals**

Two visuals. (1) Photograph/screenshot composite, boxed with a dark charcoal #2A3137 border about 2pt wide and white interior, at x 10.9% y 26.4% w 29.5% h 22.8%, not cropped, showing two smartphone app screenshots side by side. Left screenshot is the main page of a shopping app: a top category bar with Chinese characters, a large banner photo of a woman in a striped top and sunglasses headed by the Chinese characters for seasonal clothing, a grid of small round icons, and three clothing items on hangers; red arrows point from white rectangular callouts labelled Product categories, Campaigns, Sales promotion and Product recommendation; caption Main page – browsing and exploration at bottom left. Right screenshot is a product page showing a photo of a striped shirt on a model, price ¥26.8, a red-and-white buyer section with Buyer A and Buyer B rows, each with a red button, a red arrow pointing to the white callout Join an existing team initiated by another buyer, a red banner Initiate a team purchase with a red arrow, and a white box labelled Individual purchase below two red price boxes; caption Product introduction at bottom left. Dominant colours are white, red, and pastel clothing tones. Lighting is flat screen lighting. (2) Line chart, titled Active Buyers, China, with a y-axis titled Pinduoduo Active Buyers, China (unit MM, scale 0 to 500MM, labelled ticks 0, 250MM and 500MM, light grey gridlines at 250MM and 500MM and a baseline at 0), and an x-axis of quarters Q1 to Q1 grouped under years 2017 (Q1 to Q4), 2018 (Q1 to Q4) and 2019 (Q1). One series, a single green line, with values about: Q1 2017 about 68MM; Q2 2017 about 100MM; Q3 2017 about 158MM; Q4 2017 about 246MM; Q1 2018 about 294MM; Q2 2018 about 345MM; Q3 2018 about 385MM; Q4 2018 about 419MM; Q1 2019 about 443MM (the 443MM headline value is printed in the subtitle, the other values are estimates). No legend. No highlighted points; the final point is at the top-right end of the line.

**Layout**

Full-width blue title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide, with the two-line title left-aligned at about 1.9% from the left edge. Below it, three equal columns sit side by side, each with a bold centred heading, an italic centred two-line caption and a tall portrait image in a dark rectangular frame, with the images aligned on a shared top edge at about 33.5% and shared bottom edge at about 80%. A thin light-grey hairline crosses the slide at about 93% height, with the centred source line beneath it, the BOND wordmark and Internet Trends 2019 at bottom left, and the page number 72 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Three photographs, each a portrait-oriented image in a dark slate frame, displayed left to right in equal columns. (1) 40K Years Ago, Painting, Indonesia: a red-ochre cave painting on a pale cream rock surface, showing an animal figure with fine hatched fur-like strokes, a curved horn or beak-like form, and faded handprint-like shapes at the edges; dominant colours rust red, orange and cream; the image is cropped to a tall rectangle, boxed, with no overlay. (2) 5K Years Ago, Cuneiform, Mesopotamia: a photograph of a beige clay tablet pressed with rows of wedge-shaped cuneiform impressions and ruled horizontal and vertical incision lines; lit flatly with soft shadows; dominant colours sand beige and tan; cropped to a tall rectangle, boxed, no overlay. (3) 131 Years Ago, Oldest Known Moving Image, Video, United Kingdom: a high-contrast black-and-white strip of film frames arranged in four rows, each frame showing a house doorway with a window and figures walking on a lawn, separated by black film-edge bands with irregular white gaps; dominant colours black and white with grey midtones; cropped to a tall rectangle, boxed, no overlay. A small BOND wordmark logo in grey serif capitals sits at bottom left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF background, with a #00517A header band across the top 12.5% of the slide. Clean corporate style on a white background, with a dark teal-blue header band #00517A across the top and white title text. Title and column headings are dark charcoal #2A3137; captions are charcoal #2A3137 in italic; source line and page number are light grey (#BFBFBF and #A6A6A6); footer text is pale grey #C8C8C8 in Georgia serif. Title is set in Arial regular in white at about 4.4% of slide height; column headings in Arial Bold at about 3.0%; italic captions in Arial Italic at about 2.2%; footer and source text at about 1.3 to 1.5%. Image frames are dark slate #2A3137 borders of roughly 0.5% of slide width, with square corners, no shadows and no gradients.

Column 3, top: a black-and-white photograph of a 1960s-style classroom viewed from the back with rows of children at desks, a chalkboard with posters reading 'THE AGE OF DISCOVERY' and 'MULTIPLICATION FACTS', high-key even lighting, full-frame, boxed; 386 by 242 px, box at x 67.9%, y 40.4%, 25.7% by 21.4%. **Layout**

Two equal columns, each holding a centred bold heading, a grey subheading and a line chart, separated by a thin vertical divider at the slide's horizontal centre. The title sits left-aligned in a full-width dark blue band across the top, about 2% from the left edge. The footer has a thin grey rule, the BOND logo and 'Internet Trends 2019' at bottom left, a source line starting at about 27% width, and the page number '77' at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Two line charts side by side, each with a grey subheading and light grey horizontal gridlines.
Left chart: line chart titled 'Annual New Photos Taken, Global'. Y-axis titled 'Photos Taken, Global', units trillions (T), range 0 to 1.4T, labelled ticks 0, 0.7T and 1.4T. X-axis tick labels 2013, 2015, 2017 (annual data, range about 2013 to 2017). Single green series (about #34AA6E) as a 3pt line with no markers. Labelled values: none printed. Estimated values: 2013 about 0.66T; 2014 about 0.81T; 2015 about 1.0T; 2017 about 1.2T. No legend. No highlighted points.
Right chart: line chart titled 'Instagram Monthly Active Users, Global'. Y-axis titled 'MAUs, Global', units billions (B), range 0 to 1.0B, labelled ticks 0, 0.5B and 1.0B. X-axis tick labels 2010, 2014, 2018 (annual range 2010 to about 2018). Single dark blue series (#00517A) as a 3pt line with no markers. Labelled values: none printed. Estimated values: 2010 about 0; 2014 about 0.3B; 2016 about 0.6B; about 0.5B near 2015.8; line leaves the top of the plot at about 1.0B around 2017.5. No legend. No highlighted points.
A thin light grey vertical divider line runs between the two columns.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background (#FFFFFF). Title band: solid dark blue #00517A across the top 12.5% of the slide height, with white title text in Arial regular (sans-serif, normal weight), about 4.4% of slide height, two lines. Section headings in Arial Bold, about 3.3% of slide height, dark charcoal #2A3137. Chart subheadings in Arial Bold about 2.2%, light grey #BFBFBF. Axis tick and axis title labels in Arial Bold about 1.8%, light grey #BFBFBF. Source line in Arial regular about 1.3%, #BFBFBF. Page number in Arial regular about 1.5%, #A6A6A6. Footer wordmark 'Internet Trends' and '2019' in Georgia regular about 1.5%, #C8C8C8. Lines: chart gridlines hairline light grey (#E0E0E0); vertical divider 1px light grey (#BFBFBF); footer rule 1px #D9D9D9. Series: green #34AA6E on the left, dark blue #00517A on the right. No shapes with corner radii, shadows or gradients.

**Text**

People have always been visual – our brains are
wired for images. Writing was a hack, a detour.
Pictorial languages are how we all started to
communicate – we are coming full circle.
We are reverting to what is most natural.
Instagram has always been a
communication platform, not an image sharing tool.
Instagram challenges the notion that beauty
comes in a traditional, artsy form…
it’s not about beauty, it’s about the story you tell.
Instagram’s inherent feedback systems help users
continuously improve communication skills.
Kevin Systrom – Instagram Co-Founder, 5/19

**Text**

Picture or 1,000 Words? / Mallard Duckling making a running leap into the water from the rock ledge at Argyle Lake, Babylon, Long Island. Mallard ducks are the most common & / recognizable wild ducks in the Northern Hemisphere. They spend most of their time near natural bodies of water (ponds, marshes, streams, & lakes) / where they feed on plants, invertebrates, fish, and insects. Mallards are dabbling, or surface-feeding, ducks because they eat by tipping underwater for / food—head down, feet and tail in the air—rather than diving. Mallards also forage and graze for food on land. The male mallard duck, called a drake, / sports a glossy green head, a white ring around its neck and a rich, chestnut-brown breast. The mallard duck's outer feathers are waterproof, because of / an oil that’s secreted from a gland near the tail. Soon after birth, baby ducks, called ducklings, open their eyes. A little more than a day after hatching, / ducklings can run, swim, and forage for food on their own. They stay in the nest for less than a month. A group of ducklings is called a brood. Outside the / nest, the brood sticks close by the mother for safety, often following behind her in a neat, single-file line. Mallard ducks are the most common & / recognizable wild ducks in the Northern Hemisphere. They spend most of their time near natural bodies of water (ponds, marshes, streams, & lakes) / where they feed on plants, invertebrates, fish, and insects. Mallards are dabbling, or surface-feeding, ducks because they eat by tipping underwater for / food—head down, feet and tail in the air—rather than diving. Mallards also forage and graze for food on land. The male mallard duck, called a drake, / sports a glossy green head, a white ring around its neck and a rich, chestnut-brown breast. The mallard duck's outer feathers are waterproof, because of / an oil that’s secreted from a gland near the tail. Soon after birth, baby ducks, called ducklings, open their eyes. Outside the / nest, the brood sticks close by the mother for safety, often following behind her in a neat, single-file line. ### Slide 98

**Text**

…Fortnite = Voice Chat…
Collaborative Communication Capped @ 16 Squadmates
To truly see the future of collaborative gameplay & social experiences,
you need a large-scale community to help that happen.
We work really, really hard on Fortnite to maintain a safe experience online –
for example, there's only chat between you & your squadmates.
There's no proximity-based chat, so it's not possible for
one person to grief another person they don't know.
Kim Libreri – CTO, Epic Games, 3/19
Strategize / Bond With Team in
Pre-Game Lobby via Voice
Real-Time In-Game Collaboration With
Team via Voice
Source: Wired (3/19). Epic Games.
BOND
Internet Trends
2019

Above the characters, a blue shield-style icon labelled 'NinjasHyper' with a speaker icon and the word 'Ready' in green; over the right character, a flask icon labelled 'TheBoyDuddus' with a crown and speaker icon and 'Not Ready' in red. I launched [Runescape] in 2001.
The basic plan was to run it for free, but to pay for my
hobby through advertising. However, when the dot
com bubble began to collapse, advertising dried up &
there was no way to pay for the game's server.
This is how the member [subscription] came about... once we had people paying, we were able to reinvest back into the game. The more we invested, the faster it grew.

**Visuals**

Left column: two rectangular screenshots placed side by side with a grey right-pointing triangle between them. The first screenshot (about 16.4% by 22.6% of the slide, at x 8.9, y 25.0) shows an orange Fortnite promotional poster with the yellow headline PLAYING FOR FREE, the line EVERYONE CAN EARN: and a bulleted list in small white text (Hello Friend Emote, Master Portal Backbling, Snakebite Pickaxe, Glider Glider, Coral Chorus Music, And more!). A white silhouette of a standing Fortnite character with one arm raised sits on the right side, and a grey Victory Royale style shield emblem sits at top left. The second screenshot (about 15.2% by 22.5%, at x 30.3, y 24.8) is an orange game screen headed PLAYING WITH THE BATTLE PASS with a gold star emblem and a row of four small item thumbnails, plus a larger inset photo-like render of a teal armoured character with a backpack at lower right. Both screenshots have a dark charcoal #2A2F36 border about 0.5% of slide width thick, square corners, and no shadow. A grey filled right-pointing triangle (#A6A6A6) of about 6.2% by 12.6% sits between them at x 39.2, y 34.7. Right column: a line chart titled Epic Fortnite Revenue Growth, per Nielsen Superdata* in bold dark text. Source: Nexon = Annual Company Filings. HearthStone = Activision Blizzard Filings + Morgan Stanley estimates. Zynga = Zynga Annual Filings.
Rovio = Rovio Annual Reporting. Note Paid users refers to users who upgrade to unlock premium features such as ad-free game play.
Paid Users % of Total = share of payers in a period divided by total active users in the same period.

**Layout**

Full-width blue title band across the top with two-line white title left-aligned at about 2% margin. Below, a 2x2 grid of four small combo charts (Nexon top-left, HearthStone top-right, Zynga bottom-left, Rovio bottom-right) separated by thin light grey cross lines, with a centred legend under the grid, a grey footer rule with a left BOND/Internet Trends/2019 block, a centred three-line source note, and page number 104 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Four combo charts, each with dark blue bars for Paid Users on the left axis and a red line for Paid % of Total Users on the right axis, years 2015 to 2018 on the x-axis. Nexon: left axis 0 to 10MM, right axis 0% to 20%; bars about 5.0MM, 5.3MM, 6.5MM, 6.3MM; line about 10.5%, 12%, 15%, 18%. HearthStone: left axis 0 to 6MM, right axis 0% to 30%; bars about 2.4MM, 3.2MM, 3.6MM, 3.4MM; line about 19%, 22%, 24%, 27%; source note says Morgan Stanley estimates. Zynga: left axis 0 to 2MM, right axis 0.0% to 3.0%; bars about 0.95MM, 1.1MM, 1.22MM, 1.1MM; line about 1.55%, 1.95%, 2.3%, 2.1%. Rovio: left axis 0 to 1.0MM with gridline at 0.5MM, right axis 0% to 2% with gridline at 1%; bars about 0.35MM, 0.42MM, 0.57MM, 0.53MM; line about 0.3%, 0.45%, 0.8%, 0.9%. Values marked about because the slide prints no data values. Each chart has a grey left axis title Paid Users (Blue Bar) and a grey right axis title Paid User % of Total (Red Line). Legend centred below the grid: dark blue square labelled Paid Users, red line labelled Paid % of Total Users. No highlighted points.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background with a dark blue header band #00517A. Title white Arial regular, about 4.4% of slide height, two lines. Chart titles dark grey #3C434B Arial bold about 3.7% of height. Axis labels and footer text light grey #BFBFBF Arial about 1.3% to 1.5%. Bars solid #00517A with no outline. Lines red #C00000, about 0.5% of height thick, round joins. Thin light grey #D9D9D9 divider lines. No shadows, gradients or rounded corners. Page number #A6A6A6. Wordmark and subtitle in Georgia serif in light grey #C8C8C8.

### Slide 107

**Text**

Freemium Enterprise (2006) = / Google G Suite… / Free / Communicate With Others… / Your apps / From Google / Gmail / Drive and Docs / Slides / Forms / Google Admin / Search for users / Admin console / Users / Add, rename, and manage users / Company profile / Update information about your company / Premium / …Enterprise User Experience / Paid Customers* / G Suite Customers * / 6MM / 3MM / 0 / 2007 2009 2011 2013 2015 2017 2019 / Google’s many successful products deliver magical user experiences [for free] & when I joined Google, I was inspired to bring that same magic to the workplace with G Suite... / Building [free] products that are loved by billions of users has driven a discipline in the G Suite team for simplicity of design & we are bringing that billion-user experience to the workplace…you’re actually seeing that workplace users are demanding it. / Prabhakar Raghavan – Google, SVP of Engineering, 7/18 / Source: Google Cloud Disclosures (2019) for G Suite Users. Google Next Conference for quote (7/18). Note: *Customers refers to the number of paying businesses using G Suite, not the number of paid users (e.g., one company with 10K employees would be counted as one customer. Google does not disclose the average G Suite customer size.) / 106 / BOND / Internet Trends / 2019

**Layout**

A full-width dark blue title band across the top about 12.5% of the slide height, with the title in white flush left at about 2.4% from the left edge. Below it the body is split into two columns by a thin vertical divider at the slide centre: left column 'Free' with two app screenshots and a quote, right column 'Premium' with a line chart. Column headings are centred over each column. A light grey rule and a small footer sit at the bottom: BOND logo and Internet Trends 2019 at bottom left, centred source note, and page number 106 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Left column: two phone-style screenshots side by side with a grey right-pointing triangle between them. The first screenshot, 'Your apps' grid from Google, shows app tiles Gmail (red M envelope icon), Drive and Docs (multicolour triangle icon), Slides (yellow presentation icon), Forms (purple document icon), with partly visible tiles below in blue and green. The second screenshot, Google Admin console, has a blue header bar with the Google Admin wordmark and a search field, then the 'Admin console' label, and two tiles: Users (blue person icon, caption 'Add, rename, and manage users') and Company profile (multicolour building icon, caption 'Update information about your company'), with partly visible device and shield icons at the bottom. Both screenshots are boxed by thick dark charcoal (#2A3137) frames with square corners. Right column: line chart titled 'Paid Customers*' with y-axis titled 'G Suite Customers *' (vertical, grey) ranging from 0 to 6MM with gridlines labelled 0, 3MM and 6MM (units: millions of customers). X-axis years 2007 to 2019 at two-year intervals, labelled 2007 2009 2011 2013 2015 2017 2019. One green series, about 0.1MM in 2007, about 0.3MM in 2008, about 0.4MM in 2010, about 0.6MM in 2011, about 1.2MM in 2013, about 2.1MM in 2015, about 3.0MM in 2017, about 5.0MM in 2019 (values are estimates, no values printed except axis ticks). No legend, no highlighted points.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF covering the whole slide. White background with a dark teal-blue title band #00517A. Title text white regular sans-serif (Arial), about 4.4% of slide height, cap height of about 3%. Column headings 'Free' and 'Premium' in Arial Bold, charcoal #2A3137, about 3.7% of slide height. Subheadings in Arial Bold Italic, mid grey #969696, about 2.2%. Quote body text in Arial Bold Italic and Arial Italic, dark slate #3C434B, about 2.0%. Attribution in Arial Bold and Arial regular #3C434B, about 1.8%. Chart title Arial Bold #2A3137 about 2.6%. Axis labels and footnote in light grey #BFBFBF, about 1.8% (footnote 1.3%). Chart line bright green #00B050, about 0.6% of slide height thick, rounded joins. Gridlines light grey #D9D9D9, thin. Vertical divider light grey #BFBFBF, thin. Footer rule light grey. Page number Arial in #A6A6A6, about 1.5%. BOND logo in Georgia-like serif bold grey #BFBFBF; Internet Trends and 2019 in Georgia regular #C8C8C8, about 1.5%. No shadows or gradients.

**Layout**

Four equal chart panels in a 2x2 grid below a full-width blue title band, separated by a thin light-grey vertical and horizontal rule crossing at the slide centre. The title sits left-aligned in the band at top-left with a 1.9% left margin; chart titles are centred above each panel; a centred legend sits below the grid; a source footnote is centred at the bottom with the BOND logo and 'Internet Trends 2019' at bottom-left and the page number 108 at bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Four combined bar-and-line charts, one per company, each with blue bars for paid users on a left axis and a red line for paid percentage of total users on a right axis. Dropbox (top-left): x-axis 2016, 2017, 2018; left axis 0 to 18MM with gridlines at 0, 9MM and 18MM; right axis 0% to 3.0% with ticks at 0%, 1.5% and 3.0%. Bars about 8.8MM (2016), about 11.0MM (2017), about 12.7MM (2018). Red line about 1.9% (2016), about 2.1% (2017), about 2.4% (2018). Slack (top-right): x-axis 2015, 2016, 2017; left axis 0 to 4MM with gridlines at 0, 2MM and 4MM; right axis 0% to 50% with ticks at 0%, 25% and 50%. Bars about 0.57MM (2015), about 1.47MM (2016), about 2.73MM (2017). Red line about 27% (2015), about 32% (2016), about 37% (2017). Wix (bottom-left): x-axis 2016, 2017, 2018; left axis 0 to 4MM with ticks 0, 2MM and 4MM; right axis 0% to 4% with ticks 0%, 2% and 4%. Bars about 2.17MM (2016), about 2.96MM (2017), about 3.73MM (2018). Red line about 2.3% (2016), about 2.5% (2017), about 2.8% (2018). SurveyMonkey (bottom-right): x-axis 2016, 2017, 2018; left axis 0 to 0.8MM with ticks 0, 0.4MM and 0.8MM; right axis 0% to 4% with ticks 0%, 2% and 4%. Bars about 0.57MM (2016), about 0.60MM (2017), about 0.64MM (2018). Red line about 3.7% (2017) and about 3.7% (2018), with no 2016 point. Axis titles in each panel: left 'Paid Users (Blue Bar)' and right 'Paid User % of Total (Red Line)', rotated vertically. No highlighted points. Legend centred below the grid: blue square marker with 'Paid Users' and a red line sample with 'Paid % of Total Users'. No photographs or icons.

Below it, two equal columns split by a thin vertical divider at about x 50%: left column 'Free' with two app screenshots side by side above a centred italic quotation block; right column 'Paid' with a centred bar-and-line combo chart. Column headings are centred over each column. Footer rule runs full width at about y 93%, with a BOND logo block at bottom left, the source line centred, and page number 110 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Two app screenshots and a small grey arrow on the left, and one combo chart on the right. Screenshot 1 (left, about x 5.1% y 25.2%): dark-mode Spotify 'Share' sheet on a dimmed grid of album art, with a close X at top left, the title Share at top centre, and three rows with chevrons: Messages (green icon), Instagram Stories (gradient icon), Twitter (blue icon). Screenshot 2 (about x 29.5% y 25.0%): Spotify desktop home view with the Spotify logo at top left, a left sidebar listing Home, Search, Your Library, and Recently Played entries (Vampire Weekend, Little Dark Age, Release Radar, Prince, She & Him), and on the right a Your Discover Weekly card (cropped) with the label Discover and a green button. A grey right-pointing triangle sits between the screenshots. Chart titled 'Paid Users + Share of Total' (bold dark #2A3137, centred above the plot). Chart type: column (bar) with a line on a secondary axis. Left y-axis: 'Paid Users (Blue Bar)', 0 to 100MM, gridlines at 0, 50MM and 100MM. Right y-axis: 'Paid User % of Total (Red Line)', 0% to 50%, labels at 0%, 25%, 50%. X-axis categories 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018. Blue bars (about values, no printed values): 2015 about 28MM, 2016 about 48MM, 2017 about 71MM, 2018 about 96MM. Red line (about values, no printed values): 2015 about 31%, 2016 about 39%, 2017 about 44%, 2018 about 46%, plotted as a straight-segment line with no markers. No legend; the axis titles serve as the legend. Bars are dark blue, line is dark red, gridlines light grey.

**Design**

Background white #FFFFFF. Header band across the top about 12.5% of slide height in dark blue #00517A. Title text white #FFFFFF in regular Arial/Helvetica-style sans-serif, about 4.4% of slide height per line. Column headings Free and Paid in bold Arial #2A3137 at about 3.7% of slide height. Sub-headings in bold italic Arial #969696 at about 2.2%. Body quotation in bold italic and regular italic Arial #2A3137 at about 2.0%. Chart title bold Arial #2A3137 about 2.6%. Axis labels and category labels regular Arial #BFBFBF at about 1.8%. Source line bold Arial 'Source' and regular text in #BFBFBF at about 1.3%. Page number #A6A6A6 about 1.5%. BOND and Internet Trends/2019 in Georgia-style serif #C8C8C8 about 1.5%. Divider line and footer rule light grey #BFBFBF, thin (about 1 px). Bars solid #00517A with square corners, no shadows. Red line #C00000, about 3 px stroke. Screenshots have a dark grey frame and slight drop border, square corners.

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with the title left-aligned in white at the top-left margin. Below it two equal columns separated by a thin vertical grey divider at about 50% width: left column 'Free' with a photo and a centred italic quote; right column 'Paid' with a combo bar and line chart. A thin grey rule spans the width above a footer row holding the BOND logo and 'Internet Trends 2019' at bottom left, a centred source line, and the page number 111 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Left column: one photograph in a thin dark charcoal frame (about 0.3% of slide width), showing a man seen from behind and above at a wooden desk, with a tablet in the foreground displaying the Canva editor and a black design card with yellow script reading 'Adam Powell'. Scattered on the desk are a fan of colour swatches (pink, teal, white), a pair of gold scissors, a blue ink bottle, pencils in a white cup, and loose orange and teal pencils. Warm natural daylight from the upper left, dominant colours wood brown, pale lavender sleeves, pastel swatches and blue ink; uncropped rectangle with square corners and no overlay. Right column: a combo chart titled 'Monthly Active Users + Designs Created'. Blue bars use the left axis titled 'Monthly Active Users (Blue Bar)' with unit millions, range 0 to 20MM, with gridlines at 10MM and 20MM. The red line uses the right axis titled 'Monthly Designs Created (Red Line)' with unit millions, range 0 to 120MM, with ticks at 0, 60MM and 120MM. Categories on the horizontal axis are 5/16, 5/17, 5/18 and 5/19. Bar values are not printed; estimates: 5/16 about 2MM, 5/17 about 5MM, 5/18 about 11MM, 5/19 about 18MM. Line values are not printed; estimates: 5/16 about 10MM, 5/17 about 27MM, 5/18 about 55MM, 5/19 about 103MM. The line is plotted as points joined by straight segments with markers at each category. No legend; the series are identified by the axis titles and their colours. Highlighted points: none beyond the bar and line ends. Gridlines are light grey.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background. Title band and bar fill #00517A (deep teal blue). Title text white #FFFFFF in regular Arial/Helvetica sans-serif, approx 4.4% of slide height. Column headings 'Free' and 'Paid' bold Arial #4A4A4A at about 3.7% of height. Subtitles bold italic Arial #969696 at about 2.2%. Chart title bold Arial #2A3137 at 2.6%. Quote body italic Arial #3C434B at about 2.0%, centred, line spacing about 2.4% of height between lines, with blank line gaps between paragraphs. Attribution 'Melanie Perkins' bold #3C434B and rest regular at 1.8%. Axis labels and ticks Arial #BFBFBF at 1.8%. Footer 'BOND' and 'Internet Trends 2019' in Georgia serif #C8C8C8 at about 1.5%. Source line bold 'Source' and regular text #BFBFBF at 1.3%. Page number Arial #A6A6A6 at 1.5%. Red line #C00000 about 0.5% of slide width thick. Vertical divider and footer rule light grey #BFBFBF, 1px. Photo frame dark charcoal #2B2F33. No shadows, no gradients, no rounded corners.

**Layout**

Full-width solid blue title band across the top 12.5% of the slide, with two left-aligned white title lines inset about 1.7% from the left edge. Below it, a centred bold subtitle sits above a thin full-width grey rule, and two columns are split by a thin vertical grey divider at about 50% width: left column a three-row table (Gaming, Enterprise, Consumer) and right column a nine-row table with year and monetization columns. A footer rule runs across the bottom at about 93% height with a left-aligned BOND/Internet Trends block, a centred grey footnote block, and the page number 114 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

No photographs or illustrations. One small logo: the BOND wordmark (grey serif lettering, image 60 by 15 pixels) at bottom left, x 4.1%, y 94.4%. Two thin dark-grey table rules: one under the left table header area from x 8.7% to 45.3% at about y 40.1%, and one under the right table header from x 55% to 92.5% at about y 40.1%. Thin light-grey horizontal rule under the subtitle from about x 5% to 95% at y 24.3%. Thin light-grey vertical divider from y 24.4% to 87% at x 50%. No chart, no diagram. Table content: left table columns are Category (Gaming, Enterprise, Consumer), Company (Epic Games, Dropbox, Spotify) and subscribers (27MM**, 13MM, 100MM), with Epic Games marked (Private Company) beneath. Right table columns are Category, Company, $1B+ Revenue 1st Year, and Primary Monetization Drivers. Background: Solid white #FFFFFF across the whole slide, with a solid #00517A band across the top 12.5%. White background (#FFFFFF). Title band solid blue #00517A with white (#FFFFFF) Arial regular title text. Subtitle and headings Arial Bold in near-black #2A3137; 'Pure-Play' in Arial Bold Italic. ### Slide 125

**Text**

Product Development (1890s-1950s)… / IBM = Feet-on-Street Customer Input / Sales Force + Customers / IBM developed a sales force that became deeply / knowledgeable about their customers’ operations & could / explain benefits specific to each organization. / Customers became highly engaged with IBM / employees to explain what product innovations they / needed to better use these [tabulation machines] that had / become so essential to their operations. / Research & development at IBM depended on this / interaction between engineers & customers. / James Cortada – Change & Continuity at IBM, 3/18 / IBM / Annual Revenue / Revenue / $2B / $1B / $0 / 1910 / 1935 / 1960 / BOND / Internet Trends / 2019 / Source: IBM Revenue per IBM Online History Archives (Collected 2019). James W. Cortada’s ‘Change & Continuity’ at IBM: Key Themes in Histories of / IBM (Cambridge Press, Spring 2018 edition). Cimarron City Library Digital Archives. Note: Image contains a mixture of IBM sales people, engineers & / customers gathered @ IBM Corporation School for collaborative working sessions. Photo taken 1951. / 124

**Layout**

Two-column layout below a full-width dark blue title band: the left column (sales force) is centred on a vertical axis near x 30%, and the right column (IBM revenue chart) sits right of a thin vertical grey divider at about x 50%. The title is left-aligned in the band at top-left with about 2% left margin; the footer runs along the bottom with a centred source note, a BOND logo and 'Internet Trends 2019' at bottom-left, and the page number '124' at bottom-right at about x 96%, y 95%.

**Visuals**

1) Photograph (boxed, not cropped, rectangular with a thin dark border): a black-and-white group photograph of about 90 men in suits and a few women, arranged in rows on the steps in front of a stone building entrance (IBM Corporation School). The building has a recessed doorway with an ornate grille, two wall lamps, and lettering 'INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS MACHINES CORPORATION SCHOOL' above the door. A placard at the bottom reads 'CUSTOMER ADMINISTRATIVE CLASS NO.710 OCTOBER 22 1951'. Framing is a full-front, eye-level view. Lighting is even, flat daylight. Colours are greyscale. A dark frame border surrounds the image. 2) Line chart (titled 'IBM' with subtitle 'Annual Revenue'): y-axis 'Revenue' from $0 to $2B, with light grey horizontal gridlines at $0, $1B and $2B. X-axis is years 1910 to 1960, labelled 1910, 1935 and 1960. One green series (#2EAD6E, about 5 px thick, no markers). Estimated values (no values printed on the slide): about 1913 $0.01B; about 1920 $0.015B; about 1925 $0.015B; about 1930 $0.02B; about 1935 $0.02B; about 1940 $0.05B; about 1945 $0.14B; about 1950 $0.26B; about 1955 $0.69B; about 1957 $1.0B; about 1960 $1.8B. The line is nearly flat until about 1935, then rises steeply after 1950. No legend and no highlighted points. 3) Logo: small grey serif wordmark 'BOND' at bottom-left, with 'Internet Trends 2019' beneath it.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate style on a white background. The title band is dark teal-blue #00517A spanning full width at the top, about 12.5% of the slide height. Title text is white #FFFFFF in a regular-weight sans-serif (Arial), about 4.4% of slide height (about 3.2% cap height). Section headings are bold italic (Arial Bold Italic) in charcoal #2A3137 at about 3.3% of slide height. The chart heading 'IBM' is bold sans-serif #2A3137 and 'Annual Revenue' is bold grey #BFBFBF. Body text is italic sans-serif (Arial Italic) #2A3137 at about 2.0% of slide height, with bold italic for the highlighted sentence. Attribution uses Arial bold for the name and italic for the title, at about 1.7%. Chart labels and axis text are grey #BFBFBF at about 1.8%. The chart line is green #2EAD6E. The photo has a dark charcoal #2A3137 frame. The vertical divider is a thin light grey #D9D9D9 line. The footer rule is a thin light grey #E5E5E5 horizontal line. Footer source text is grey #BFBFBF at about 1.3%. The BOND wordmark is grey, and the 'Internet Trends 2019' text is light grey #C8C8C8 in a Georgia-style serif. The page number is grey #A6A6A6. Shapes have square corners, with no shadows or gradients.

**Text**

Segment + Meredith = Manage Connections to…
Organize Customer Data Across IT Systems
Segment = Customer Data Infrastructure
Segment
Annual Recurring Revenue
Today’s customers expect highly relevant,
contextualized experiences wherever they interact with
a business. However, this is an extremely difficult
technology problem to solve.
Businesses are interacting with customers across
dozens of digital channels, leading to a tangled mess
of data that is siloed throughout their organization.
Customer Data Infrastructure solves this problem.
It allows companies to collect, manage & easily
route their first-party data to whichever application
requires it, ensuring customer experiences are
consistent and relevant.
Peter Reinhardt – Segment, Co-Founder / CEO, 6/19

Segment has enabled us to streamline
the customer data capture process,
while maintaining flexibility to customize
for each of our 36+ magazine brands as needed.
Before adopting Segment, we were spending far too
much money on disjointed analytics & we had
no way to look at the entire network at scale…
We now look across the entire organization to make sure
we’re best serving all of these groups.
Grace Preyapongpisan & Kerry-Anne Doyle –
Meredith, Business Intelligence, 1/18

Four elements. **Layout**

Two-column grid split by a thin vertical grey rule at about x 50% and a thin horizontal grey rule at about y 53% running from x 5% to 95%, forming four quadrants: top-left Confluent text and diagram, top-right Confluent line chart, bottom-left Accor text and screenshot, bottom-right Accor line chart. A full-width dark blue title band sits across the top 12.5% with two left-aligned white title lines starting at x 1.8%. Quadrant headings are centred over their columns. A footer rule runs across the slide near y 93%, with the BOND wordmark and Internet Trends 2019 at bottom left, the source line centred at bottom, and the page number 142 right-aligned at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Four visuals. (1) Diagram, top-left, boxed image (311 by 161 px) at x 3.5%, y 29.0%: a black-outlined rectangle enclosing a white diagram. Across the top are six small grey line icons with tiny captions (about: Same Day Transaction Processing, Fare Changes & Billing, Real-Time Customer 360, Machine Learning Models, Real-Time Data Transformation, Real-Time Fraud Detection). Below them, vertical arrows point up to a wide white rounded pill with a black outline labelled CONFLUENT, centred. Under the pill, further vertical arrows connect to small rounded rectangles labelled about Custom Apps, Splunk, Device Logs, and Web Apps, plus two cylinder database icons and small captioned boxes; the labels are too small to read exactly. (2) Line chart, top-right, titled Confluent, subtitle Annual Bookings. X axis years 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 with light grey labels; no y-axis values or units printed; no legend. One green series (about #00B050) with no printed values: starts near the baseline at 2014, about flat to 2015, rises gently to 2016, bends up at 2017, and climbs steeply to the top-right end at 2018. Horizontal light-grey gridlines at about three levels. Hidden white labels 0x, 3x and 6x sit at the left of the chart in white on white, so they are not visible. (3) Screenshot, bottom-left, boxed image (284 by 169 px) at x 4.2%, y 67.2%: a black-outlined rectangle showing a web page with a white background. At top is the ACCOR HOTELS wordmark with a small logo, then a navigation row: HOTELS (underlined), VILLAS & HOMES, RESTAURANTS, MEETINGS & EVENTS. Centre-left is the serif headline The finest hotels at the best prices. Below are the labels Where do you travel?, a text input with placeholder Destination, Hotel name, and date fields Check-in and Check-out with calendar icons, then a centred yellow SEARCH button. (4) Line chart, bottom-right, titled Accor, subtitle Monthly Requests for Lodging Availability. Y axis from 0 to 6B with labelled ticks 0, 3B and 6B (units: billions of requests). X axis labelled 1/16, 1/17, 1/18, 1/19. One dark navy series (#00517A) with no printed values; about 1.3B at 1/16, about 2.3B at 1/17, about 4.1B at 1/18, about 4.4B at 1/19, with a steep middle segment. No legend; no highlighted points. Light-grey gridlines at 0, 3B and 6B. (5) Small BOND wordmark logo at bottom left, serif grey, with a thin rule.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate look. Title band is a solid dark teal-blue (#00517A) with white sans-serif regular titles (Arial) about 4.4% of slide height, the main title line sitting above a second line of similar size. Quadrant headings are bold sans-serif (Arial Bold) about 3.0% of slide height in charcoal #2A3137. Quadrant subheadings are bold Arial about 2.0% in light grey #BFBFBF. Body quotes are Arial italic about 1.5% of slide height in charcoal #2A3137, with bold italic emphasis on key phrases. Attributions are Arial about 1.1%, with the name in bold. Chart axis labels are Arial about 1.5% in light grey #BFBFBF. Footer uses Georgia in #C8C8C8 for BOND and Internet Trends 2019, source line Arial in #BFBFBF about 1.3%, page number Arial in #A6A6A6. Lines are thin light grey (#BFBFBF, about 1 px), chart lines about 4 px thick, no shadows or gradients, no rounded corners apart from the Confluent pill, and screenshot and diagram images have heavy dark outlines (#2A3137, about 3 px).

### Slide 157

**Text**

Data Volume + Utilization… / Technology Change > Human Adaptability / Humans’ ability to adapt to / technological change is increasing, / but it is not keeping pace with the speed / of scientific & technological innovation. / To overcome the resulting friction, / humans can adapt by developing / skills that enable faster learning & / quicker iteration & experimentation. / Developing these skills is particularly important / for policy makers & regulators who are looking / to protect the public interest. They need to be / ready to try new approaches, iterate & / change with the times so tech progress / goes hand in hand with public benefit. / Astro Teller – X, The Moonshot Factory / Adapted from Thomas Friedman’s Thank You For Being Late, 2016 / Rate of Change / Time / Technology / We Are / Here / Potential Human / Adaptability Acceleration / Owing to Faster Learning & / Smarter Regulation / Human / Adaptability / 156 / BOND / Internet Trends / 2019 / Source: Adapted from quotes originally appearing in ‘Thank you For Being Late’ by Thomas Friedman, 2016. Updated in June 2019 by Astro Teller.

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band runs across the top of the slide with a two-line white title left-aligned at the left margin. Below it, a two-column layout: a centred italic text block on the left, a thin vertical grey divider at about 50% width, and a line chart on the right occupying roughly 52% to 94% of the width. The attribution sits centred under the text block. A thin grey rule runs across the footer, with the BOND logo at lower left, the source line centred-left and the page number 156 at lower right.

**Visuals**

Line chart with no title. X-axis labelled Time (no units, no numeric ticks, axis unlabeled by values); y-axis labelled Rate of Change (no units, no numeric ticks). Both axes are thin dark grey (#2A3137) lines of about 1 pt, forming an L shape with the origin at lower left. Series 1, Technology: thick bright green (#00B050) curve, about 4 pt, rising slowly then steeply exponentially from lower left near (59%,75%) to upper right near (89.5%,32%); no values printed. Series 2, Human Adaptability: thick dark navy (#00517A) curve, about 4 pt, nearly flat rising gently from about (59%,65%) to about (89.5%,58%); no values printed. Highlighted point: solid dark charcoal (#2A3137) dot about 1.5% of slide width at about (77%,58%) where the green curve crosses above the navy curve, with a thin black arrow (about 1 pt) pointing to it from the label We Are Here above-left. Dashed red (#FF0000) thin line, about 0.5 pt, running from about (76%,62%) diagonally up-right to about (83%,55%), indicating the potential acceleration gap between the curves. Legend: none; the series are identified by direct labels Technology (green) and Human Adaptability (navy). A thin light grey vertical divider line (#A6A6A6, about 0.5 pt) at x about 50%, from y about 23% to 83%. The BOND logo at lower left is a small grey serif wordmark, about 4% wide, in grey (#A6A6A6 to #C8C8C8). No photographs, icons or other images.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White slide background with a full-width dark teal header band (#00517A) covering the top 12.5% of the slide height. Title text is white (#FFFFFF) regular sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica), about 4.4% of slide height per line, which is large relative to the body. Body text is dark charcoal (#2A3137) Arial, bold italic for the first and second paragraphs at about 2.6% of slide height and regular italic for the third paragraph at the same size, centred. Attribution is Arial at about 1.85% with the name in bold. Chart labels are Arial bold: Technology in green #00B050 at 2.2%, Human Adaptability in navy #00517A at 2.2%, We Are Here in charcoal #2A3137 at 2.2%. Red annotation text (#FF0000) is Arial regular at about 1.5%, centred. Footer source line is light grey (#BFBFBF) Arial at 1.3%, with the book title in italic. Page number in #A6A6A6 Arial at 1.5%. Logo text in Georgia-like serif in #C8C8C8. No shadows, gradients or corner radii; lines are square-ended.

**Layout**

Full-width solid dark-blue title band across the top about 12.5% of the slide height, with the two-line left-aligned title inside it. Below, a centred two-line bold italic subtitle sits above a horizontal bar chart: category labels right-aligned in a column at the left (bracketed into a green 'Better / Positive' group and a maroon 'Worse / Negative' group), the zero axis at about 62.5% of slide width, and two outlined arrow callouts ('More Negative' left, 'More Positive' right) beneath the chart. A thin grey rule runs across the full width above a footer with the BOND logo and Internet Trends text at lower left, a centred source line, and the page number 161 at lower right.

**Visuals**

Horizontal bar chart (diverging bar chart). Title: 'Do Social Media Platforms You Use Make These Health-Related Factors Better or Worse?' No axis tick values or numeric axis labels are printed; the horizontal axis runs from 'More Negative' (left) to 'More Positive' (right) with a vertical dark zero line at about 62.5% of slide width and light grey vertical gridlines at about 38.1, 44.2, 50.3, 56.4, 68.7, 74.8, 80.9 and 87.0% of slide width. Single series, 15 categories top to bottom, values about: Self-Expression about +20 (bar to 82.4%), Self-Identity about +15, Community Building about +14, Emotional Support about +13, Awareness of Others about +11, Access To Health Info about +5, Real-World Relationships about +3.5, Loneliness about +0.5, Average about +0.3 (green bars, positive side); Depression about -4.5 (bar from 57.9%), Anxiety about -7, Body Image about -12.5, Bullying about -14, Fear of Missing Out about -16.5, Sleep Quality / Amount about -23.5 (red bars, negative side, longest bar). Values are estimates, as no values are printed. Bars are solid, flat, with no data labels; green #00B050 for positive, red #C00000 for negative. Legend: none; the colour groups are labelled by the 'Better / Positive' (green) and 'Worse / Negative' (red) brackets. Highlighted points: none beyond colour coding. Two outlined block arrows below the chart: left arrow outlined red 'More Negative', right arrow outlined green 'More Positive'. Two bracket frames at left: green outlined frame around the first eight categories (Self-Expression to Loneliness) and maroon frame around the Depression to Sleep Quality group. A small BOND logo (grey serif wordmark) at lower left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, with a dark teal-blue #00517A title band across the top 12.5%. White background with a dark teal-blue header band (#00517A) across the top. Title text white, regular-weight Arial-style sans-serif, about 4.4% of slide height per line. Subtitle and group labels bold italic sans-serif (Arial Bold Italic), dark slate #2A3137 for subtitle and category labels, with green #00B050 for 'Better / Positive' and red #C00000 for 'Worse / Negative'. Category labels bold Arial, about 2.2% of slide height. Arrow callout labels in bold Tahoma, about 2.6%. Source text light grey #BFBFBF, about 1.3%. Bars flat with no shadows or gradients; gridlines thin light grey (#D9D9D9); zero axis line thin dark slate. Bracket frames have about 0.4% thick strokes in dark green (#00703C) and maroon (#8B1A3C). Arrow outlines about 0.1% stroke, no fill. No rounded corners or shadows anywhere.

**Layout**

Two equal columns sit below a full-width navy title band across the top, separated by a thin light-grey vertical divider at about 50% of the slide width. The title is left-aligned at about 1.9% from the left edge, inside the band. The left column holds a line chart and the right column holds a grouped bar chart, each with a centred bold heading above it. A thin horizontal rule runs across the full width at about 93% of the slide height, below which sit the source line, the BOND logo block at lower left and the page number at lower right.

**Visuals**

Two charts. (1) Left chart: line chart titled '% of Adults Trying to Limit Personal Smartphone Use, USA'. Y axis titled '% of Respondents, USA', range 0% to 70% with gridlines at 0%, 35% and 70%. X axis categories 2017 and 2018. One series in green #00B050 running from 47% at 2017 to 63% at 2018, plotted as a straight line about 3 pt thick with no markers; both values are printed as labels, 47% below-left of the start point and 63% above the end point, in bold green. No legend. No highlighted points beyond the labelled endpoints. (2) Right chart: clustered column chart titled 'Parent Actions to Regulate Children’s Internet / Phone Usage'. Y axis titled '% of Parent Respondents, USA', range 0% to 60% with gridlines at 0%, 30% and 60%. Two categories: 'Used Digital Parental Controls for Websites' and 'Used Digital Parental Controls for Phone Use'. Series 2015 in light grey #D9D9D9 and series 2018 in navy #00517A. Values: Websites 2015 = 39% (about 39%, printed label), Websites 2018 = 52%; Phone 2015 = 16%, Phone 2018 = 57%. Value labels sit above each column in dark grey #2A3137. Legend below the category labels: grey square 2015, navy square 2018. Source attribution 'Pew Survey (USA)' printed in light grey below the legend. Bars are about 4.9% of slide width each, with a small gap between the two bars in each cluster. The BOND logo is a small wordmark image, 60 by 15 pixels, grey serif text reading BOND, with 'Internet Trends 2019' beneath it.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF background across the whole slide. Clean corporate report style. Title band in solid navy #00517A across the top 12.5% of the slide height, with white title text in a regular-weight sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica-like), about 4.4% of slide height per line, two lines, left-aligned. Chart headings and category labels are bold dark slate #2A3137 sans-serif (Arial Bold-like) at about 2.6% of slide height for headings and about 2.0% for category labels. Axis tick labels and axis titles are light grey #BFBFBF sans-serif at about 1.8% of slide height. Body and value labels are regular sans-serif in #2A3137. Accent colours: navy #00517A for the 2018 bars, green #00B050 for the line series and its labels, light grey #D9D9D9 for 2015 bars and gridlines. Gridlines are thin light grey lines about 0.75 pt. The vertical divider and the horizontal footer rule are thin light grey #D9D9D9 lines. No shadows, gradients, rounded corners or icons. Footer text is small grey: source line in #BFBFBF at about 1.3% of slide height, page number in #A6A6A6 at about 1.5%. Apple: Screen Time settings sheet on white with a blue Cancel link, bold title, four rows with small coloured square icons (purple hourglass for Weekly Reports, purple moon for Downtime and App Limits, red circle with slash for Content and Privacy Restrictions, blue padlock for Screen Time Passcode) and a full-width blue #007AFF Continue button. Google: Digital Wellbeing screen on pale mint background with a multicolour donut ring showing 3 hr 22 min Today, with labelled segments Other, YouTube, Chrome, Gmail, Messages, Drive and Calendar; below it 215 Unlocks and 112 Notifications, then a settings list. Facebook: Your Time on Facebook screen with a blue #4267B2 header bar, a column chart of seven days S M T W T F S with pale blue bars and the W bar in saturated blue highlighted, a dark tooltip reading 58 min over the W bar, values for other bars not printed (about 40 to 50 minutes, estimated), then Manage Your Time and Manage Your Notifications rows with a bell icon and chevron. YouTube: Time watched screen on white with a stats list Today 34 minutes, Yesterday 38 minutes, Past 7 days 4 hr 5 minutes, Daily average 35 minutes, and toggles: Remind me to take a break off in grey, Autoplay next video on in blue #065FD4.
